props.gloss_en: the mishna: in the week in which 9 Av falls, cutting hair and laundering are forbidden
the mishna: and on Thursday they are permitted, for the honour of Shabbat
they taught [the prohibition] only of laundering and wearing; but laundering and setting aside is permitted
Rav Sheshet: even laundering and setting aside is forbidden
Rav Sheshet: know it -- for the launderers of Rav's house were idle
the Thursday clause actually permits laundering and wearing, and speaks of one who has only one shirt
R' Yochanan: one who has only one shirt may launder it on chol hamoed
the baraita: it is forbidden to launder before 9 Av, even to set aside until after 9 Av
and our fine-laundering is like their laundering
and linen garments have no [prohibition] of fine-laundering
R' Yochanan: although they said linen has no [issue of] fine-laundering, it is forbidden to wear it in the week in which 9 Av falls
Rav: they taught [the prohibition] only before it [9 Av]; after it, it is permitted
Shmuel: even after it, it is also forbidden
the baraita: if [9 Av] falls on Sunday, it is permitted to launder the whole week
on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday: before it forbidden, after it permitted
if it falls on Friday, it is permitted to launder on Thursday, for the honour of Shabbat
and if he did not launder on Thursday, it is permitted to launder on Friday from mincha onward
Abaye (and some say Rav Acha bar Yaakov) cursed [one who does] this
if [9 Av] falls on Monday or Thursday, three read [the Torah] and one is maftir
on Tuesday or Wednesday, one reads and the same one is maftir
R' Yosei: always three read and one is maftir
Shmuel [could] tell you: it is a dispute of tannaim
the baraita: 9 Av that falls on Shabbat, and likewise the eve of 9 Av that falls on Shabbat -- he eats and drinks all he needs and sets on his table even [a meal] like Solomon's in his time
R' Meir: cutting hair and laundering are forbidden from Rosh Chodesh until the fast
R' Yehuda: the whole month is forbidden
RSBG: it is forbidden only that week alone
the other baraita, R' Meir: mourning is observed from Rosh Chodesh until the fast
R' Yehuda: the whole month is forbidden
RSBG: it is forbidden only that week alone
R' Yochanan: all three expounded one verse, as it is written 'I will cause all her mirth to cease, her festival, her new moon and her Shabbat' (Hos 2:13)
the one who said from Rosh Chodesh until the fast -- from 'her festival'
and the one who said the whole of it is forbidden -- from 'her new moon'
and the one who said the whole week is forbidden -- from 'her Shabbat'
Rava: the halakha follows RSBG
and Rava said: the halakha follows R' Meir
and both [rulings] are for leniency
had he taught only 'the halakha follows R' Meir', I would say [forbidden] even from Rosh Chodesh; so he taught 'the halakha follows RSBG' [the prohibition starts only in that week]
and had he taught only 'the halakha follows RSBG', I would say [forbidden] even after it; so he taught 'the halakha follows R' Meir' [the prohibition ends at the fast]
